Article 6

(1) Forms of violence against Women and Children include physical, sexual, economic and psychological.

(2) Forms of physical violence are any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causes death.

(3) Forms of sexual violence are sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial and/or certain purposes. (4) Forms of economic violence are neglect of family members in the form of not providing proper livelihood, care or maintenance.

(5) Forms of psychological violence are acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

Article 3

The Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence aims to provide protection and services to women against gender-based violence and the best interests of children occurring in households or public.

Article 2

The Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is carried out based on respect and recognition of equal human rights and dignity, non-discrimination, gender equality and justice as well as protection of the human rights of women and children and the best interests of victims.

Article 7

(1) Every woman and child who becomes a victim of violence must receive protection in accordance with applicable provisions. (2) Protection of women and children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) is provided to the population of Sumenep Regency whether committed in Sumenep or outside Sumenep.

(3) Protection of women and children victims of violence in addition to being provided to the population of Sumenep as referred to in paragraph (2), also applies to non-residents of Sumenep committed within the territory of Sumenep Regency.

Article 8

(1) Forms of protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include medical, legal, medicolegal (forensic medicine), economic and psychological protection.

(2) The form of medical protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1) is in the form of treatment and recovery of physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical and paramedical personnel free of charge.

(3) The form of legal protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1) is in the form of services and assistance to help victims undergo legal and judicial processes.

(4) The form of medicolegal protection for Women and Children. Victims of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1) is in the form of medical services for evidentiary purposes in the legal field. (5) The form of economic protection for Women and Children. Victims of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1) is in the form of services for skills and providing economic access so that victims can be independent.

(6) The form of psychological protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1) is in the form of assistance in order to restore the traumatic condition of victims including the provision of safe houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation for victims and provide psychological support so that victims have self-confidence, strength and independence in solving problems.

Article 5

(1) The Implementation of Protection for victims is carried out in an integrated manner within the P2TP2A framework.

(2) P2TP2A in handling medical, legal, medicolegal, psychological and economic protection in its implementation may partner with community social institutions engaged in the protection of women and children.

(3) The implementation of protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) must take into account religious norms as well as the rights and obligations of parents, guardians, husbands/other persons who are legally responsible for the victim. (4) The mechanism for handling protection as referred to in paragraph (1) is stipulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 4

(1) The Regent through the Regional Apparatus establishes a public service work unit that functions as P2TP2A.

(2) The Regional Apparatus as referred to in paragraph (1) in implementing the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence may coordinate with other Regional Apparatus.
